handoff: Approve: one day-file line reader with observer, type-first writes, typed skip by prefix with older-line fallback; norn trace output unchanged (TIMELINE_TYPES matches traceEntries). Typecheck + 1244 tests green. Non-blocking: blockedHookCount now quiet on unreadable files; AC2 S1 half trivially green; TIMELINE_TYPES hand-kept. AC4 for QA.

findings.title: blockedHookCount now silently ignores an unreadable day file
findings.detail:
Before, blockedHookCount read each day file with readFileSync and threw on any read error (only an unlistable dir was ignored). It now passes `quiet: true`, so an EACCES/EISDIR day file is skipped and the count is lower. In line with readHookFacts' diagnostic-trace treatment, but a behaviour change the slice does not mention.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Keep it (and say so in the doc comment: diagnostic, never fatal), or drop `quiet` for this reader.

findings.title: AC2's "`norn trace` does not report the line" cannot fail at S1
findings.detail:
`norn trace` never surfaced readTrace errors, so the cli test's `after.stdout === before.stdout` passes with or without the skip. The skip itself is proven at S2 (config-trace: typed reader reports no error for the broken tick.start line). The handoff states this.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: None needed; QA should note that the S1 half of AC2 is satisfied trivially.

findings.title: TIMELINE_TYPES is a mutable hand-kept list with no compile-time link to traceEntries
findings.detail:
A new trace type that traceEntries starts showing must also be added to TIMELINE_TYPES, or `norn trace` silently drops it. The array is also exported mutable.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: `readonly` and a comment at traceEntries' switch pointing at TIMELINE_TYPES (or a test that every type traceEntries maps to a non-empty list is in it).
